title: Model Architecture Manifest
description: Statically-extracted ground truth about a model's learned architecture. Every fact carries a source_ref and confidence; unresolved values MUST be the string "unknown".

adapter_selection.description: How the family adapter was chosen. Recorded because selection strength is itself a fact about the manifest's reliability: a match on a config-key signature alone is weaker than a match on the family's own class names, and the reader cannot tell which happened from `adapter` alone.

candidates.description: Every adapter whose signature fired, including the losers. An ambiguous top tier is an error, never resolved silently, so this list documents that only one adapter reached it.

capabilities.description: Family capabilities this source actually evidences. Validators gate family-specific rules on these (see check_dataflow D7), so a Dense model is never asked to have MoE branches. An absent capability means unknown-or-absent and asserts nothing.

dataflow_invariants.description: Declarative dataflow constraints the family adapter asserts, evaluated by check_dataflow. Carried here rather than hardcoded in the checker: a checker holding its own family table cannot abstain for a family it has never seen. Only invariants whose gating capability is evidenced appear.

requires.description: The capability id that gates this rule; null means ungated.

kind.description: Generic checker operation; omitted defaults to parallel_join.

reason.description: What goes wrong in the breakdown if the constraint is violated.

component_candidates.description: Submodules each layer class declares in __init__, as CANDIDATES for the mapper. Not a decomposition: __init__ order is not execution order and a declared submodule may never be called, so containment and dataflow are decided against forward() (extract_dataflow.py).

role_candidates.description: Proposed semantic roles for declared submodules. Every entry is confidence='low' with the naming hint that produced it, because a name is evidence of intent and not of behaviour. `unresolved` lists attributes no hint matched -- left unassigned on purpose so the mapper sees what still needs deciding instead of inheriting a default.

known_deviations.description: Constructs this family is known to defeat static extraction on. Recorded so the gap is visible here rather than surfacing downstream as an unexplained abstention.

weights_config_sha256.description: SHA256 of the deployed checkpoint config selected for this manifest.

facts.description: Every extracted scalar architecture fact with provenance.

evidence_gaps.description: Human-readable list of things that could not be resolved statically.

capture_provenance.description: How much of this capture's architecture claim is bound to evidence, as opposed to read off source that may or may not describe the run. Set by detect_capture_provenance(); consumed by score_breakdown.py to decide which checks are runnable and which denominator the score is out of.

tier.description: S0 = model defined in-repo with random weights, so source is the only truth. S = source snapshot + capture manifest + step marks, so source is bound to this trace. A = source present but not bound to the capture. B = no source. C = neither source nor a usable capture.

checkpoint_config.description: Where the scalar hyperparameters (num_hidden_layers and friends) come from. Level 4 means an AST default argument nothing confirms, which is why it raises an evidence gap rather than being treated as a fact.

evidence_level.description: 1 = checkpoint config.json, or self-defined source that is itself the truth. 2 = a runtime record (log/summary) that states the value. 2S = an AST default bound to the capture by a source snapshot. 3 = reserved. 4 = an unbound AST default argument.

id.description: e.g. moe / shared_expert / mtp / mla / sparse_index_attention / sliding_window_attention

evidence_keys.description: What evidences this capability: config keys resolved to a truthy value, or the class names that declare it (see source_ref for which channel). Required and non-empty: a capability with no evidence is an assertion, and asserting one turns on validation rules the source never justified. A key present but resolving to None/False/0 is the source saying the feature is off, and does not appear here.

source_ref.description: `config:<key>:<line>` when a config value evidences it, `class:<ClassName>` when a module in the modeling source does.

type.description: Source class name, optionally suffixed (e.g. DeepseekV3DecoderLayer_dense)

count_config_key.description: Config key that governs count, e.g. num_nextn_predict_layers
